card.name: Subject word before a verb phrase
card.fires_on: A noun or small word that sits right before a verb phrase, such as 'This risk' before 'may occur', 'influence' before 'and activity', or 'may' after a drug name. It is strongest in the NSAID cardiovascular warning.

modes.label: Risk statement subject
modes.description: The word 'risk' after 'This' in the NSAID cardiovascular thrombotic warning, just before 'may occur'.
modes.example: AIDs) cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, including myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal. This<< risk>> may occur early in treatment and may increase

modes.label: Modal after drug subject
modes.description: The word 'may' placed right after a drug name that is the subject of a sentence.
modes.example: .5 Angle Closure Glaucoma The pupillary dilation that occurs following use of many antidepressant drugs including desvenlafaxine extended-release tablets<< may>> trigger an angle closure attack in a patient

modes.label: General prose
modes.description: A word like 'to' or 'influence' in general historical prose, where a clause continues after it.
modes.example: Court’s decision a decade earlier in the already-notorious case of Dred Scott, which said blacks “had no rights which the white man was bound<< to>> respect.” They trusted Congress—and amended the
